paper.title_en: Reduced Gravitational Wave Signal Reopens the Ultralight Primordial Black Hole Window
paper.abstract_en: The hot big bang may have emerged from evaporation of primordial black holes (PBHs) lighter than <math display="inline"><mrow><msup><mrow><mn>10</mn></mrow><mrow><mn>9</mn></mrow></msup><mtext> </mtext><mtext> </mtext><mi mathvariant="normal">g</mi></mrow></math>. Standard monochromatic treatments predict nearly simultaneous evaporation, abrupt reheating, and a large poltergeist scalar-induced gravitational wave signal. We confront this expectation with the irreducible collapse mass tail predicted by general relativity, <math display="inline"><mrow><mi>d</mi><msub><mrow><mi>f</mi></mrow><mrow><mi>PBH</mi></mrow></msub><mo>/</mo><mi>d</mi><mi>ln</mi><mi>M</mi><mo>∝</mo><msup><mrow><mi>M</mi></mrow><mrow><mn>3.78</mn></mrow></msup></mrow></math>, which smooths reheating, suppresses the signal by orders of magnitude, and reopens the ultralight PBH window.
